kings2.5.p1.b1.text: Now Naaman, the commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man in his master’s sight and highly regarded, for through him the LORD had given victory to Aram. And he was a mighty man of valor …

kings2.5.p1.b3.text: If only my master would go to the prophet who is in Samaria, he would cure him of his leprosy.

kings2.5.p2.b1.text: Go now … and I will send you with a letter to the king of Israel.

kings2.5.p2.b2.text: So Naaman departed, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold, and ten sets of clothing.

kings2.5.p2.b3.text: Am I God, killing and giving life, … Surely you can see that he is seeking a quarrel with me!

kings2.5.p3.b1.text: Why have you torn your clothes? Please let the man come to me, and he will know that there is a prophet in Israel.

kings2.5.p3.b2.text: Go and wash yourself seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will be restored, and you will be clean.

kings2.5.p3.b3.text: I thought that he would surely come out … Are not the Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?

kings2.5.p4.b1.text: My father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more, then, when he tells you, ‘Wash and be cleansed’?

kings2.5.p4.b2.text: So Naaman went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God …

kings2.5.p4.b3.text: … and his flesh was restored and became like that of a little child, and he was clean.

kings2.5.p5.b1.text: Now I know for sure that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. So please accept a gift from your servant.

kings2.5.p5.b2.text: As surely as the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will not accept it.

kings2.5.p6.b1.text: If you will not … please let me, your servant, be given as much soil as a pair of mules can carry. For your servant will never again make a burnt offering or a sacrifice to any other god but the LORD.

kings2.5.p6.b2.text: Yet may the LORD forgive your servant this one thing: When my master goes into the temple of Rimmon to worship there, and he leans on my arm, … may the LORD forgive your servant in this matter.

kings2.5.p7.b1.text: But after Naaman had traveled a short distance …

kings2.5.p7.b2.text: Look, my master has spared this Aramean, Naaman, while not accepting what he brought. … I will run after him and get something from him.

kings2.5.p7.b4.text: Everything is all right … My master has sent me to say, ‘I have just now discovered that two young men from the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two sets of clothing.’

kings2.5.p7.b5.text: When Gehazi came to the hill, he took the gifts from the servants and stored them in the house. Then he dismissed the men, and they departed.

kings2.5.p8.b2.text: Your servant did not go anywhere

kings2.5.p8.b3.text: Did not my spirit go with you when the man got down from his chariot to meet you? Is this the time to accept money and clothing, …

kings2.5.p8.b4.text: Therefore, the leprosy of Naaman will cling to you and your descendants forever!

kings2.5.p8.b5.text: And as Gehazi left his presence, he was leprous—as white as snow.
